FINDINGS -- two, both real, neither vacuating a gate.

FINDING 1 (MEDIUM, new file added by this PR). scripts/lwb_check_foreign_repo.py:329 references an undefined name. In _run_hook's JSONDecodeError/IndexError handler the f-string is `f"FAIL: hook stdout was not valid JSON for command {command!r}"`, but the parameter is `tool_command` (and the launched string is `launch_command`); there is no module-level `command`. REPRODUCTION: make the shipped hook print a non-JSON line and exit 0, then run the script -- instead of the intended FAIL message you get `NameError: name 'command' is not defined` and a traceback. Empty stdout with exit 0 reaches the same line via the IndexError arm. The job still goes RED (EXIT=1) and the scratch repo is still cleaned up by the `finally`, so this is NOT a vacuous check -- but the one handler whose whole job is to say "the hook did not produce a decision" cannot say it. The sibling scripts/lwb_check_hook_launch.py gets the same case right (it appends a correct message and continues). Worth fixing before this file accumulates users.

FINDING 2 (LOW-as-shipped, but an unscoped claim). The commandWindows half of BLOCKER 1 was applied to scripts/lwb_check_hook_launch.py only. scripts/lwb_check_foreign_repo.py -- added in the same PR, and also run on windows-latest by the new lwb-foreign-repo job -- reads the whole hook dict for `timeout` but then launches `bash_entry["command"]` unconditionally; the string "commandWindows" does not appear in the file at all (verified by grep across the repo: it appears in lwb_check_hook_launch.py, lwb_validate_codex_plugin.py, .codex/hooks.json, plugins/codex/lwb/hooks/hooks.json, docs, and proof/27.json -- never in lwb_check_foreign_repo.py). This is latent today, because the Claude plugin's Bash entry declares no commandWindows; it becomes live the moment one is added, and it is precisely the shape the commit message says it was fixing ("read the whole hook dict ... the way lwb_check_foreign_repo.py's _bash_hook_entry already does" -- true of `timeout`, not of `commandWindows`). Consequently proof/27.json's acceptance criterion "commandWindows is launched on Windows when hooks.json declares one, rather than always launching command" (met: true) is stated without scope; it is true of lwb_check_hook_launch.py and false of lwb_check_foreign_repo.py. Read in sequence after the criterion that names lwb_check_hook_launch.py explicitly, the scoped reading is defensible, so I am recording this as an imprecision plus a latent gap, not as a false claim. This repo's own history of scoped fixes declared repo-wide is why I am naming it rather than letting it pass.

RESIDUALS I measured but do not count against this PR (recording rather than resolving):
- A `proof` path that EXISTS but is a regular file (not a directory) makes Path.rglob return [] with no OSError, so it is reported as "0 record(s) found" -- "could not check" folded into "checked, found nothing" once more, in the one sub-case the facts_incomplete work does not cover. Consequence is only a spurious warn (a repo in that state can hold no records anyway), so it is minor, but it is the same family the PR set out to close.
- `{"mode": null}` in a policy resolves to OFF with no degraded marker, because raw_cfg.get("mode") cannot tell an explicit null from an absent key. The code comment deliberately treats an absent mode as the ordinary case; an explicit null rides along on that. Very low.
- scripts/lwb_check_hook_launch.py still prints the single cheerful line "lwb-portable check passed" with no counts, while its sibling added by this PR prints what it proved. The PR touched this file; the asymmetry is now visible.
- The Codex plugin's bin/lwb_hook.py carries none of the fail-open-never-silent surfacing (policy unreadable/degraded, repo facts unavailable/incomplete) that the Claude one gained. d85cc34's own message discloses this as out of lane per CLAUDE.md, so it is disclosed, not hidden. Separately, plugins/codex/lwb/hooks/hooks.json registers only an "Agent" matcher and the Codex adapter ships no repo_facts module, so lwb_proof_required cannot fire under Codex at all -- pre-existing, not this PR's doing.
